title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: SBD > MR > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture of a winter‑70 show, anchored by an epic Dark Star → St Stephen → The Eleven run and solid overall set.
ai_review.review: The recording is a decent‑to‑good sound‑board source that lets Jerry’s guitar sit front‑and‑center while the room’s natural bass response adds warmth.  Musically the show shines with a towering Dark Star/St Stephen/The Eleven sequence, a tasty Mason’s Children → High Time segue and a lively Lovelight, though a few listeners find Mason’s Children weak or cut short.  Overall the set flows smoothly, balancing jam‑heavy moments with classic ballads.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance 4–5 stars and praise the Dark Star and overall set, while noting only minor recording glitches; the strong show weight (70%) outweighs the good‑but‑imperfect sound quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear with Jerry’s guitar prominent and a natural bass “amp” feel; occasional hiss, tape‑speed quirks and short cuts (e.g., Mason’s Children) are mentioned but do not dominate the listening experience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid winter‑70 set that blends mellow ballads with high‑energy jams; the second set builds to a peak with Dark Star > St Stephen > The Eleven and finishes on Lovelight, delivering a satisfying arc despite a few missing or trimmed moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is nicely out front, described as perfect tone, likely an SG; his playing is highlighted throughout the Dark Star and jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass locks in with Jerry during The Eleven jam; no major criticism noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig (Tom Constanten) on keys receives praise for sweet organ work; a note that TC may have left shortly after this period.
